items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: I'm not trying to knock Dave Stewart, he's a wonderful guy and a good friend

ctx.x: He was dead in that two summer.

Well, yeah, the next summer, that was the fall of 1940, and he died in June. But he was talking how at that time he was still going to sue either MCA or he was suing ASCAP. He was always suing somebody for a million dollars, not paying royalties on his tunes. I mean, he had big ideas like that, exaggerated some things of that kind of, he wouldn't have been due a million dollars royalty, but he figured a lot of people were cashing in on his work, which they did. They never got to be millionaires, of course, but…
Well he said don't leave me here. He said he's always had six, seven, eight, or nine. Yeah, that's right. Yeah. Maybe they just gave him some.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: he got a letter from Dave Stewart that Dave was going to come over here and record Bunk... Gene decided then to come down too... they decided that Dave would better do the recording issue

ctx.x: Well, we own all that. Who was Gene Williams? And I never did quite know how he got in the picture and when and when. Was he in the book?

No, he's not. No, he was a student at Columbia University along with Ralph Gleason and a couple other people he knew like Barry Olenov is that his name, the one-time editor of Metronome and Tori Dano was another of his friends there. So I know Gleason's talked about how he started reviewing, Gleason began reviewing records for the Columbia College paper just so he could get free records, I guess, from the companies mostly. And Gene probably did some of that work too. Anyway, Gene started about as soon as he was…
Speaking about Bunk Johnson, how many people were involved really in his coming back? Was there quite a group of people interested in him? I know you played a large part.
